newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Storm over PLO security chief's settler blast.
newsitem.headline: Storm over PLO security chief's settler blast.

text.p: Jewish settlers and the Israeli defence establishment were up in arms on Sunday after a PLO security chief said settlers had no place in Hebron.
Jibril Rajoub, the head of Yasser Arafat's police in the West Bank, said he stuck by his statement that 400 armed Jewish settlers did not belong in Hebron.
"I said Hebron was not a natural place for these settlers and I stick by that," Rajoub told Reuters on Sunday after Arafat's arrival in the city.
Rajoub said in speech to Hebron residents on Saturday that the settlers should leave.
"These are harsh words of incitement and verbal violence that constitute a gross violation of the agreement that Jibril Rajoub personally played a part in achieving," an Israeli security source said.
"The security apparatus warned this morning that comments like these are bound to harm implementation of the agreement," the source said.
Settler leaders in Hebron called for Rajoub's dismissal.
"The first thing Arafat should do is dismiss Rajoub," settler David Wilder said, calling Rajoub's speech incitement.

The controversy highlights the problems faced by the deal, struck after U.S. pressure, between Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The agreement leaves 400 settlers and about 20,000 Arabs under Israeli control in the centre of the city around the tomb of Abraham, which is holy to Jews and Moslems.
The rest of Hebron's 100,000 residents are policed by Palestinians but they will still rub shoulders with the settlers at key points in the city.
Rajoub, a native of Hebron, told Reuters that the settlers' aim was to provoke trouble.
"The settlers here have planted the seed of hatred because of their provocations," he said.
Palestinians complain of daily harassment by the settlers who live in several enclaves near Abraham's tomb and the casbah. Some 5,000 more settlers live on the edge of Hebron.
Rajoub and other PLO commanders said their forces would protect settlers and enforce the law.
"We will punish any Palestinian who violates the law and any policeman who maltreats Palestinians will also be punished," he said. Rajoub plans to move to Hebron from Jericho.
Colonel Gadi, Israel's brigade commander in Hebron whose last name cannot be published, said animosity could not be easily overcome.
"Hebron has very tough, bad memories that go back a long way. I think it will take a long time to create different ways of thought," he told Israel Radio.
In February 1994, settler Baruch Goldstein from the nearby Kiryat Arba settlement massacred 29 Arabs kneeling in prayer at al-Ibrahimi mosque before survivors beat him to death.
In 1929 Arab rioters opposed to rising Jewish immigration killed 67 Jews.
